translations.idiomatic: Timber was gathered in Xiang Province for the main hall; at Niuzhu Jetty the raft sank entirely; later fishermen saw it floating at sea.

sentences.zh: 起齊雲觀，國人歌曰：「齊雲觀，寇來無際畔。

translations.literal: When the Equal-to-Heaven Watchtower was raised the people sang: "Equal-to-Heaven Watchtower—when invaders come there is no shore to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Equal-to-Heaven Watchtower rose the people sang, "Equal-to-Heaven Watchtower—when invaders come there is no shore to meet them."

sentences.zh: 」始北齊末，諸省官人多稱省主，未幾而滅。

translations.literal: At the end of Northern Qi many provincial officials called themselves "department lords"; before long that state perished.
translations.idiomatic: At Northern Qi's end many officials called themselves "department lords"; soon that state perished.

sentences.zh: 至是舉朝亦有此稱，識者以為省主，主將見省之兆。

translations.literal: Now the whole court also used this title; the knowing took "department lord"—lord about to be extinguished—as a portent of the ruler's fall.
translations.idiomatic: Now the whole court used the same title; the knowing read "department lord" as omen that the ruler would be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝謂僕射高熲曰：「我為百姓父母，豈可限一衣帶水不拯之乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui said to Vice Director Gao Jiong: "I am father and mother to the people—how can I be stopped by a strip of water and not save them?
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen told Vice Director Gao Jiong, "I am father and mother to the people—how can a strip of water keep me from saving them?"

sentences.zh: 」命大作戰船。

translations.literal: He ordered great warships built on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered warships built on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 人請密之，隋文帝曰：「吾將顯行天誅，何密之有！

translations.literal: When men asked that it be kept secret, Emperor Wen of Sui said: "I mean to execute Heaven's punishment in the open—what need of secrecy!
translations.idiomatic: When men urged secrecy he said, "I mean to execute Heaven's punishment openly—what need of secrecy!

sentences.zh: 使投柿于江，若彼能改，吾又何求。

translations.literal: Let persimmons be thrown into the river; if they can reform, what more do I ask.
translations.idiomatic: Throw persimmons in the river; if they reform, what more do I ask."

sentences.zh: 」及納梁蕭瓛、蕭岩，隋文愈忿，以晉王廣為元帥，督八十總管致討。

translations.literal: When Liang's Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan were received, Sui's wrath grew fiercer; Prince of Jin Guang was made commander-in-chief and eighty area commanders were ordered to punish Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan were received, Sui's wrath sharpened; Prince Guang became commander-in-chief and eighty area commanders marched against Chen.

sentences.zh: 乃送璽書，暴後主二十惡。

translations.literal: He then sent an imperial letter enumerating the Later Lord's twenty crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an imperial letter listing the Later Lord's twenty crimes.

sentences.zh: 又散寫詔書，書三十萬紙，遍喻江外。

translations.literal: Edicts were also copied and scattered—three hundred thousand sheets—to announce them throughout the lands beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were copied and scattered—three hundred thousand sheets—throughout the lands beyond the river.

sentences.zh: 諸軍既下，江濱鎮戍相繼奏聞。

translations.literal: Once the armies descended, garrison after garrison along the river reported in succession.
translations.idiomatic: As armies descended, river garrisons reported one after another.

sentences.zh: 新除湘州刺史施文慶、中書舍人沈客卿掌機密，並抑而不言。

translations.literal: The newly appointed governor of Xiang Province Shi Wenqing and Secretariat Gentleman Shen Keqing held the secrets of state and suppressed the reports.
translations.idiomatic: New Xiang governor Shi Wenqing and Secretariat Gentleman Shen Keqing held state secrets and suppressed the reports.

sentences.zh: 初蕭岩、蕭瓛之至也，德教學士沈君道夢殿前長人，朱衣武冠，頭出欄上，攘臂怒曰：「那忽受叛蕭誤人事。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan and Xiao Kan first arrived, the Virtue-Teaching scholar Shen Jundao dreamed of a tall man before the hall in crimson robes and martial cap, his head above the railing, who rolled up his sleeves in rage and said: "How dare you accept the renegade Xiao and ruin affairs!
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan and Xiao Kan arrived, Virtue-Teaching scholar Shen Jundao dreamed of a tall crimson-robed man before the hall, head above the railing, who rolled up his sleeves and raged, "How dare you accept renegade Xiao and ruin affairs!"

sentences.zh: 」後主聞之，忌二蕭，故遠散其眾，以岩為東揚州刺史，瓛為吳州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord heard this he came to fear the two Xiao and therefore dispersed their followers far away, making Yan governor of Eastern Yang and Kan governor of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this the Later Lord feared the two Xiao, dispersed their followers, made Yan governor of Eastern Yang and Kan governor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 使領軍任忠出守吳興郡，以襟帶二州。

translations.literal: He sent Camp Commandant Ren Zhong to guard Wuxing commandery to hold the two provinces as a strategic belt.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Camp Commandant Ren Zhong to guard Wuxing as strategic belt for the two provinces.

sentences.zh: 使南平王嶷鎮江州，永嘉王彥鎮南徐州。

translations.literal: He sent Prince Yan of Nanping to garrison Jiang Province and Prince Yan of Yongjia to garrison Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Yan of Nanping to garrison Jiang Province and Prince Yan of Yongjia to garrison Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 尋召二王赴期明年元會，命緣江諸防船艦，悉從二王還都為威勢，以示梁人之來者，由是江中無一斗船。

translations.literal: Soon he summoned the two princes for the New Year's assembly of the coming year and ordered all river-defense ships to follow the two princes back to the capital to display might, showing the Liang men who came; hence not a single fighting boat remained on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he summoned both princes for next year's New Year court and ordered all river-defense ships to follow them back as a show of force for arriving Liang men—leaving not one fighting boat on the river.

sentences.zh: 上流諸州兵，皆阻楊素軍不得至。

translations.literal: Troops of the upper provinces were all blocked by Yang Su's army and could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-province troops were all blocked by Yang Su and could not arrive.

sentences.zh: 都下甲士尚十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Armored men in the capital still numbered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Armored men in the capital still exceeded a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 及聞隋軍臨江，後主曰：「王氣在此，齊兵三度來，周兵再度至，無不摧沒。

translations.literal: When they heard Sui armies had reached the river the Later Lord said: "Our royal aura is here; Qi armies came three times and Zhou armies twice, and all were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Sui had reached the river the Later Lord said, "Our royal aura is here; Qi came thrice and Zhou twice, and all were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 虜今來者必自敗。

translations.literal: These barbarians who come now will surely defeat themselves.
translations.idiomatic: These barbarians will surely defeat themselves."

sentences.zh: 」孔範亦言無渡江理。

translations.literal: Kong Fan also said there was no logic to crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan also said crossing the river was impossible.

sentences.zh: 但奏伎縱酒，作詩不輟。

translations.literal: They merely presented entertainers, poured wine, and never ceased composing poems.
translations.idiomatic: They only staged entertainers, poured wine, and never stopped composing poems.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月乙丑朔，朝會，大霧四塞，入人鼻皆辛酸。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, yichou, first day of the month, of the third year, at the court assembly great fog closed in on all sides; entering people's noses it was all sour and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, spring, first month, yichou, new moon: at court assembly fog closed every side; in the nose it was sour and sharp.

sentences.zh: 後主昏睡，至晡時乃罷。

translations.literal: The Later Lord slept in a stupor until the hour of shen before the session ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord slept through until the hour of shen before court ended.

sentences.zh: 是日，隋將賀若弼自北道廣陵濟，韓擒趨橫江濟，分兵晨襲採石，取之。

translations.literal: That day Sui general He Ruobi crossed from Guangling on the northern route and Han Qin hurried to cross at Hengjiang; they divided forces at dawn, raided Caishi, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: That day Sui general He Ruobi crossed from Guangling north and Han Qin from Hengjiang; at dawn they raided and took Caishi.

sentences.zh: 進拔姑孰，次於新林。

translations.literal: They advanced to take Gudu and halted at Xinlin.
translations.idiomatic: They took Gudu next and halted at Xinlin.

sentences.zh: 時弼攻下京口，緣江諸戍望風盡走，弼分兵斷曲阿之沖而入。

translations.literal: When Ruobi attacked and took Jingkou, the river garrisons fled at the sight of his banners; Ruobi divided forces to cut the Qū'e pass and enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruobi took Jingkou the river garrisons fled at his banners; he divided forces, cut the Qū'e pass, and entered.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，採石戍主徐子建至告變。

translations.literal: On bingyin Xu Zijian, commander of Caishi garrison, arrived to report the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Caishi commander Xu Zijian arrived with the alarm.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，乃下詔曰：「犬羊陵縱，侵竊郊畿，蜂蠆有毒，宜時掃定，朕當親禦六師，廓清八表，內外並可戒嚴。

translations.literal: On wuchen an edict was issued: "Dogs and sheep run rampant, violating and stealing the suburbs; wasps and scorpions have poison—it is time to sweep them clear. I shall personally lead the Six Armies to cleanse the Eight Regions; within and without, all shall stand on alert.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen an edict ran: "Dogs and sheep run wild, violating the suburbs; wasps and scorpions are venomous—it is time to sweep them clear. I shall lead the Six Armies to cleanse the Eight Regions; all shall stand alert."

sentences.zh: 」於是以蕭摩訶為皇畿大都督，樊猛為上流大都督，樊毅為下流大都督，司馬消難、施文慶並為大監軍，重立賞格，分兵鎮守要害，僧尼道士盡皆執役。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiao Mohé was made Grand Commander of the Imperial Domain, Fan Meng commander of the upper stream, Fan Yi commander of the lower stream, Sima Xiaonan and Shi Wenqing both Grand Army Overseers; reward schedules were renewed, forces divided to guard key points, and monks, nuns, and Daoist priests were all pressed into labor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xiao Mohé became Grand Commander of the Imperial Domain, Fan Meng upper-stream commander, Fan Yi lower-stream commander, Sima Xiaonan and Shi Wenqing Grand Army Overseers; rewards were renewed, key points garrisoned, and monks, nuns, and Daoists pressed into labor.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賀若弼攻陷南徐州。

translations.literal: On gengwu He Ruobi stormed Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu He Ruobi stormed Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 辛未，韓擒又陷南豫州。

translations.literal: On xinwei Han Qin also took Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Han Qin also took Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 隋軍南北道並進。

translations.literal: Sui armies advanced on both northern and southern routes.
translations.idiomatic: Sui armies advanced on both routes.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，賀若弼進軍鍾山，頓白土岡之東南，眾軍敗績。

translations.literal: On xinsi He Ruobi advanced on Zhongshan and encamped southeast of Baitu Hill; the armies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi He Ruobi advanced on Zhongshan and camped southeast of Baitu Hill; the armies were routed.

sentences.zh: 弼乘勝進軍宮城，燒北掖門。

translations.literal: Ruobi pressed the victory toward the palace city and burned the North Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ruobi pressed victory toward the palace and burned the North Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 是時，韓擒率眾自新林至石子岡，鎮東大將軍任忠出降擒，仍引擒經朱雀航趣宮城，自南掖門入。

translations.literal: At that time Han Qin led troops from Xinlin to Shizi Hill; Garrison-East Grand General Ren Zhong came out to surrender to Qin, then led Qin along the Zhuque ferry toward the palace and entered by the South Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Then Han Qin came from Xinlin to Shizi Hill; Garrison-East Grand General Ren Zhong surrendered to Qin, led him along the Zhuque ferry to the palace, and entered by the South Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 城內文武百司皆遁出，唯尚書僕射袁憲、後合舍人夏侯公韻侍側。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of a hundred offices within the city all fled; only Yuan Xian, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Rear-Chamber Gentleman Xiahou Gongyun waited at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials all fled; only Vice Director Yuan Xian and Rear-Chamber Gentleman Xiahou Gongyun waited at his side.

sentences.zh: 憲勸端坐殿上，正色以待之。

translations.literal: Xian urged him to sit upright in the hall with stern mien and await them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian urged him to sit upright in the hall with stern mien and wait.

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「鋒刃之下，未可及當，吾自有計。

translations.literal: The Later Lord said: "Under naked blades one cannot face them; I have my own plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord said, "Under naked blades one cannot face them; I have my own plan."

sentences.zh: 」乃逃于井。

translations.literal: He then fled into a well.
translations.idiomatic: He fled into a well.

sentences.zh: 二人苦諫不從，以身蔽井，後主與爭久之方得入。

translations.literal: The two men remonstrated bitterly but he would not listen; they shielded the well with their bodies, and only after long struggle did he get in.
translations.idiomatic: The two remonstrated bitterly; he would not listen; they shielded the well with their bodies, and only after long struggle did he enter.

sentences.zh: 沈後居處如常。

translations.literal: Consort Shen remained in her quarters as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shen remained as usual in her quarters.

sentences.zh: 太子深年十五，閉合而坐，舍人孔伯魚侍焉。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince Shen, fifteen years old, sat behind closed doors; Gentleman of the Household Kong Boyu attended him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shen, fifteen, sat behind closed doors; Gentleman Kong Boyu attended.

sentences.zh: 戍士叩合而入，深安坐勞之曰：「戎旅在塗，不至勞也。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers knocked and entered; Shen sat calmly and said in courtesy: "Armies on campaign—no need to trouble yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison soldiers knocked and entered; Shen sat calmly and said, "Armies on the road—no need to trouble yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」既而軍人窺井而呼之，後主不應。

translations.literal: Then soldiers peered into the well and called to him; the Later Lord did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Then soldiers peered into the well and called; the Later Lord did not answer.

sentences.zh: 欲下石，乃聞叫聲。

translations.literal: They meant to drop stones; then they heard cries.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to drop stones; then they heard cries.

sentences.zh: 以繩引之，驚其太重，及出，乃與張貴妃、孔貴人三人同乘而上。

translations.literal: They pulled him up with a rope; startled at the great weight, when he came out it was he together with Noble Consort Zhang and Noble Consort Kong riding up on the rope.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him with a rope; startled at the weight—when he emerged it was he with Noble Consorts Zhang and Kong all three on the rope.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聞之大驚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui was greatly alarmed when he heard it.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen was greatly alarmed when he heard.

sentences.zh: 開府鮑宏曰：「東井上于天文為秦，今王都所在，投井其天意邪。

translations.literal: Bao Hong, Commissioner with the Grand Precedence of the First Order, said: "The Well asterism in the heavens corresponds to Qin; now the royal capital stands there—is casting oneself into a well Heaven's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Bao Hong said, "The Well asterism corresponds to Qin; the royal capital stands there—is leaping into a well Heaven's intent?"

sentences.zh: 」先是江東謠多唱王獻之桃葉辭，云：「桃葉復桃葉，度江不用烜，但度無所苦，我自接迎汝。

translations.literal: Earlier in Jiangdong many sang Wang Xianzhi's Peach-Leaf song: "Peach leaf upon peach leaf, crossing the river needs no punt—just cross without hardship; I myself will come to meet you.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiangdong sang Wang Xianzhi's Peach-Leaf song: "Peach leaf upon peach leaf, crossing the river needs no punt—just cross without hardship; I myself will come to meet you."

sentences.zh: 」及晉王廣軍於六合鎮，其山名桃葉，果乘陳船而度。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang's army was at Liuhe garrison the mountain there was named Peach Leaf, and indeed they crossed on Chen boats.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang's army camped at Liuhe the mountain was named Peach Leaf, and indeed they crossed on Chen boats.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，晉王廣入據台城，送後主於東宮。

translations.literal: On bingxu Prince of Jin Guang entered and held Taitai city and sent the Later Lord to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Prince Guang entered Taitai city and sent the Later Lord to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 三月己巳，後主與王公百司，同發自建鄴，之長安。

translations.literal: In the third month, jisi, the Later Lord together with princes, dukes, and officials of a hundred offices set out from Jiankang for Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, jisi: the Later Lord with princes, dukes, and officials set out from Jiankang for Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝權分京城人宅以俟，內外修整，遣使迎勞之，陳人謳詠，忘其亡焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui temporarily divided residences of Chang'an's people to await them, repaired inside and out, and sent envoys to welcome and comfort them; Chen people sang praises and forgot they had perished.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen requisitioned Chang'an residences to await them, repaired all within and without, and sent envoys to welcome them; Chen people sang and forgot their ruin.

sentences.zh: 使還奏言：「自後主以下，大小在路，五百里累累不絕。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned they reported: "From the Later Lord downward, great and small on the road, for five hundred li they stretched on without break.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys returned reporting, "From the Later Lord downward the road for five hundred li was unbroken."

sentences.zh: 」隋文帝嗟歎曰：「一至於此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui sighed and said: "To come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen sighed, "To come to this."

sentences.zh: 」及至京師，列陳之輿服器物於庭，引後主於前，及前後二太子、諸父諸弟眾子之為王者，凡二十八人；

translations.literal: When they reached the capital Chen's carriages, robes, and implements were arrayed in the courtyard; the Later Lord was led forward together with the former and latter two crown princes, imperial uncles, imperial younger brothers, and the many sons enfeoffed as kings—twenty-eight men in all;
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Chen's carriages, robes, and gear were arrayed in the courtyard; the Later Lord was led forward with former and latter crown princes, imperial uncles, younger brothers, and enfeoffed sons—twenty-eight in all;

sentences.zh: 司空司馬消難、尚書令江總、僕射袁憲、驃騎蕭摩訶、護軍樊毅、中領軍魯廣達、鎮軍將軍任忠、吏部尚書姚察、侍中中書令蔡征、左衛將軍樊猛，自尚書郎以上二百餘人，文帝使納言宣詔勞之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Sima Xiaonan, Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zong, Vice Director Yuan Xian, Cavalry General-in-Chief Xiao Mohé, Protector Fan Yi, Central Camp Commander Lu Guangda, Garrison General Ren Zhong, Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yao Cha, Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat Cai Zheng, and General of the Left Guard Fan Meng, together with more than two hundred men from Masters of Writing gentlemen upward—Emperor Wen had the Chief Counselor proclaim an edict of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Sima Xiaonan, Director Jiang Zong, Vice Director Yuan Xian, Cavalry General-in-Chief Xiao Mohé, Protector Fan Yi, Central Camp Commander Lu Guangda, Garrison General Ren Zhong, Director of Personnel Yao Cha, Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director Cai Zheng, and General of the Left Guard Fan Meng, with more than two hundred from Masters of Writing gentlemen upward—the Chief Counselor proclaimed consolation.

sentences.zh: 次使內史令宣詔讓後主，後主伏地屏息不能對，乃見宥。

translations.literal: Next the Palace Secretary proclaimed an edict reproaching the Later Lord; the Later Lord lay prostrate, holding his breath, and could not reply, yet was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Palace Secretary reproached the Later Lord; he lay prostrate breathless and could not answer, yet was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝詔陳武、文、宣三帝陵，總給五戶分守之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui ordered the mausoleums of Chen's Wu, Wen, and Xuan emperors each given five households to guard them in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen ordered the mausoleums of Chen's Wu, Wen, and Xuan each given five rotating guard households.

sentences.zh: 既見宥，隋文帝給賜甚厚，數得引見，班同三品。

translations.literal: After pardon Emperor Wen gave lavish gifts and often summoned him; his court rank matched the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: After pardon Sui Emperor Wen gave lavish gifts, often summoned him, and ranked him with the third grade.

sentences.zh: 每預宴，恐致傷心，為不奏吳音。

translations.literal: At each feast, fearing grief, he had no Wu music performed.
translations.idiomatic: At each feast, fearing grief, he forbade Wu music.

sentences.zh: 後監守者奏言：「叔寶雲，'既無秩位，每預朝集，願得一官號'。

translations.literal: Later the guards reported: "Shubao says, 'Having no rank, yet attending every court assembly, I wish to receive an office title.'"
translations.idiomatic: Later guards reported, "Shubao says, 'Without rank yet attending every court, I wish an office title.'"

sentences.zh: 」隋文帝曰：「叔寶全無心肝。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui said: "Shubao is utterly without heart or liver.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen said, "Shubao is utterly without heart or liver."

sentences.zh: 」監者又言：「叔寶常耽醉，罕有醒時。

translations.literal: The guards also said: "Shubao is constantly sunk in drink and rarely sober.
translations.idiomatic: Guards also said, "Shubao is constantly drunk and rarely sober."

sentences.zh: 」隋文帝使節其酒，既而曰：「任其性；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui ordered his wine restricted; afterward he said: "Let his nature have its way;
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen restricted his wine, then said, "Let his nature have its way;

sentences.zh: 不爾，何以過日。

translations.literal: otherwise, how would he pass the days.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise how would he pass the days."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，帝又問監者叔寶所嗜。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor again asked the guards what Shubao loved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again asked the guards what Shubao loved.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「嗜驢肉。

translations.literal: They replied: "He loves donkey meat.
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Donkey meat."

sentences.zh: 」問飲酒多少？

translations.literal: He asked how much he drank?
translations.idiomatic: He asked how much he drank.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「與其子弟日飲一石。

translations.literal: They replied: "With his sons and younger brothers he drinks a shi a day.
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "With sons and brothers he drinks a shi a day."

sentences.zh: 」隋文帝大驚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及從東巡，登芒山，侍飲，賦詩曰：「日月光天德，山川壯帝居，太平無以報，願上東封書。

translations.literal: When he followed on the eastern tour and ascended Mang Mountain to attend a feast, he composed a poem: "Sun and moon shine Heaven's virtue; mountains and rivers strengthen the Emperor's seat; in great peace nothing repays it—I wish to submit a petition for the Eastern Peak rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern tour ascending Mang Mountain for a feast he composed: "Sun and moon shine Heaven's virtue; mountains and rivers strengthen the throne; in great peace nothing repays—I wish to submit a petition for the Eastern Peak rite."

sentences.zh: 」並表請封禪，隋文帝優詔謙讓不許。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting the feng and shan rites; Emperor Wen graciously declined in an edict and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting feng and shan; Sui Emperor Wen graciously declined by edict.

sentences.zh: 後從至仁壽宮，常侍宴，及出，隋文帝目之曰：「此敗豈不由酒；

translations.literal: Later when he followed to Renshou Palace he often attended feasts, and on leaving Emperor Wen looked after him and said: "This ruin—is it not from wine?
translations.idiomatic: Later at Renshou Palace he often attended feasts; on leaving Sui Emperor Wen looked after him and said, "This ruin—is it not from wine?

sentences.zh: 將作詩功夫，何如思安時事。

translations.literal: You spend your effort on composing poems—how does that compare with thinking how to settle affairs in peace.
translations.idiomatic: You spend effort on poems—how does that compare with settling affairs in peace.

sentences.zh: 當賀若弼度京口，彼人密啟告急，叔寶為飲酒，遂不省之。

translations.literal: When He Ruobi crossed Jingkou someone secretly reported the emergency, yet Shubao was drinking and therefore did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruobi crossed Jingkou someone secretly reported the emergency, yet Shubao was drinking and never read it.

sentences.zh: 高熲至日，猶見啟在床下，未開封。

translations.literal: On the day Gao Jiong arrived the report was still under the bed, unopened.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gao Jiong arrived the report still lay under the bed unopened.

sentences.zh: 此亦是可笑，蓋天亡也。

translations.literal: This too is laughable—surely Heaven was destroying Chen.
translations.idiomatic: This too is laughable—surely Heaven destroyed Chen.

sentences.zh: 昔苻氏所征得國，皆榮貴其主。

translations.literal: In old times when Fu Jian conquered states he always honored and ennobled their rulers.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian conquered states he always honored their rulers.

sentences.zh: 苟欲求名，不知違天命，與之官，乃違天也。」

translations.literal: If one seeks a name without knowing that it violates Heaven's mandate, giving them office is itself violating Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a name while violating Heaven's mandate—giving them office violates Heaven itself."

sentences.zh: 隋文帝以陳氏子弟既多，恐京下為過，皆分置諸州縣，每歲賜以衣服以安全之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui, because Chen's clansmen were many, feared excess in the capital and therefore dispersed them to various provinces and commanderies, each year granting clothes to keep them secure.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chen clansmen were many, Sui Emperor Wen feared trouble in the capital and dispersed them to provinces and commanderies, granting clothes yearly for their security.

sentences.zh: 後主以隋仁壽四年十一月壬子，終於洛陽，時年五十二。

translations.literal: The Later Lord died at Luoyang on renzi of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Renshou of Sui at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord died at Luoyang, Sui Renshou 4, eleventh month, renzi, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍，封長城縣公，諡曰煬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Changcheng, and styled with the posthumous name Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand General, enfeoffed Duke of Changcheng, and styled Yang posthumously.

sentences.zh: 葬河南洛陽之芒山。

translations.literal: He was buried on Mang Mountain south of the Yellow River in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on Mang Mountain south of the Yellow River in Henan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳宣帝器度弘厚，有人君之量。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Emperor Xuan of Chen had a broad and generous disposition and the measure of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Chen Emperor Xuan had broad magnanimity and a ruler's measure.

sentences.zh: 文帝知塚嗣仁弱，早存太伯之心，及乎弗悆，咸已委託矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen knew the heir was mild and weak and early harbored the heart of Taibo; when illness came all had already been entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew the heir was mild and weak and early held Taibo's heart; when illness came all was already entrusted.

sentences.zh: 至於纘業之後，拓土開疆，蓋德不逮文，智不及武，志大不已，晚致呂梁之敗，江左日蹙，抑此之由也。

translations.literal: As for after he continued the enterprise and expanded territory and opened frontiers, his virtue did not reach Wen's and his wisdom did not match Wu's; his ambition knew no stop, and in his later years he met defeat at Lüliang; the lands east of the river daily narrowed—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: After continuing the enterprise he expanded borders, yet his virtue fell short of Wen's and his wisdom of Wu's; ambition unchecked, he met Lüliang defeat in old age and the east-of-river lands daily narrowed—here was the cause.

sentences.zh: 後主因削弱之餘，鍾滅亡之運，刑政不樹，加以荒淫。

translations.literal: The Later Lord, inheriting a weakened remnant and meeting the fortune of extinction, did not establish penal rule and added to it dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord inherited weakness and the fortune of extinction, established no penal order, and added dissipation.

sentences.zh: 夫以三代之隆，曆世數十，及其亡也，皆敗於婦人。

translations.literal: Even the grandeur of the Three Dynasties, passing through dozens of generations, at their fall all were ruined by women.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Three Dynasties' grandeur, passing dozens of generations, at fall were ruined by women.

sentences.zh: 況以區區之陳，外鄰明德，覆車之跡，尚且追蹤叔季，其獲支數年，亦為幸也。

translations.literal: How much more for tiny Chen, neighboring a bright virtue—tracks of overturned carts were still followed in the manner of the final age; that it lasted several years more was also fortune.
translations.idiomatic: How much more tiny Chen, neighbor to bright virtue—still tracing overturned-cart tracks in the final age's manner; that it lasted several years was also luck.

sentences.zh: 雖忠義感慨，致慟井隅，何救麥秀之深悲，適足取笑乎千祀。

translations.literal: Though loyal righteousness moved men to grief at the well's corner, what could it save of the deep sorrow of wheat bending in the wind—it only supplied laughter for a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Though loyal grief at the well's corner moved men, what could it save of wheat-bending sorrow—it only supplied laughter for a thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 始梁末童謠云：「可憐巴馬子，一日行千里。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang a children's rhyme said: "Pitiable Ba horse lad, in one day he travels a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang's end a children's rhyme ran: "Pitiable Ba horse lad, in one day travels a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 不見馬上郎，但見黃塵起。

translations.literal: One sees no lad upon the horse, only yellow dust rising.
translations.idiomatic: One sees no lad upon the horse, only yellow dust rising.

sentences.zh: 黃塵汙人衣，皁莢相料理。

translations.literal: Yellow dust stains men's clothes; black pods attend to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow dust stains men's clothes; black pods attend to one another."

sentences.zh: 」及僧辯滅，群臣以謠言奏聞，曰：僧辯本乘巴馬以擊侯景，馬上郎，王字也，塵謂陳也；

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian was destroyed the assembled ministers reported the rhyme to the throne, saying: Sengbian originally rode a Ba horse to strike Hou Jing; "lad upon the horse"—the character for king; dust means Chen;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian fell ministers reported the rhyme: Sengbian rode a Ba horse against Hou Jing; "lad upon the horse" means the character wang; dust means Chen;

sentences.zh: 而不解皁莢之謂。

translations.literal: yet they did not understand what black pods meant.
translations.idiomatic: yet they did not understand black pods.

sentences.zh: 既而陳滅于隋，說者以為江東謂羖羊角為皁莢，隋氏姓楊，楊，羊也，言終滅于隋。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Chen was destroyed by Sui, interpreters held that in Jiangdong goat horns were called black pods; the Sui clan surname was Yang, and yang means sheep—thus saying it would ultimately perish to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell to Sui, interpreters said Jiangdong called goat horns black pods; Sui's surname was Yang, yang meaning sheep—thus ultimate destruction by Sui.

sentences.zh: 然則興亡之兆，蓋有數云。

translations.literal: Thus the omens of rise and fall surely have their number.
translations.idiomatic: Thus omens of rise and fall surely have their allotted number.
